notes.title: “Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood…”
notes.intro: In his “bread of life” teaching, Jesus speaks of eating his flesh and drinking his blood. Traditions differ on how this relates to Communion.

views.label: A direct teaching about the Eucharist
views.summary: Catholic and Orthodox Christians read these words as pointing to receiving Christ’s true body and blood in the Eucharist.

views.label: About Communion and faith together
views.summary: Lutherans and many Anglicans see a connection to the Lord’s Supper while stressing that Christ is received by faith.
views.source: Formula of Concord, Solid Declaration VII

views.label: A picture of believing in Christ
views.summary: Many Protestants read “eating” as believing in Jesus, noting verse 63 (“the Spirit gives life; the flesh profits nothing”) and verse 35 (“whoever believes in Me will never thirst”).
